platform: macOS arm64; Qt 6.11.2; production protocol unchanged

review_threads.disposition: Unknown senders after binding remain non-actionable, including during reconnect replay. Retain per-sender event/byte accounting, not payloads that cannot be adopted; release accounting upon classification. Tests cover request/resolution ID collisions, delayed metadata, 1030 temporary lifecycles, both overflow bounds, and a confirmed second persistent thread.
Retain exact qualified method/code/thread-specific upstream error matching. Prefix/contains could retry unrelated failures or a different thread; a new binary must requalify this contract.
Replace QString UTF-8 roundtrip with Qt QByteArray::isValidUtf8().
Retain bounded fail-closed send semantics and nodiscard. Retry/automatic resend is deliberately outside the private observer transport contract; document it.
Reserve maximum frame header plus payload and mask into the allocated buffer.
Retain terminal failure when a control reply cannot be queued, bounded to 2 MiB; recovery must reconcile rather than accumulate another retry queue.
Accept registered close codes 1012, 1013 and 1014 while rejecting reserved on-wire codes; cover close diagnostics and echoes.
Installed Qt 6.11.2 QArrayDataOps::erase advances the data pointer for prefix removal. The claimed per-frame memmove is not present; preserve bounded receive loop.
Retire old fake server sockets and disconnect their handlers when replacing or disconnecting; cover reconnect isolation.
Handle masked extended-length frames in test decoding with regression payloads across length boundaries.
Remove redundant inner attachment guard in publish_attention while preserving the outer check.

Retain full executable SHA-256 qualification. Actual Qt hashing of the 314160568-byte installed binary measured 1238.7-1287.2 ms with OS caches left intact. Service ready-ack timer begins afterward; desktop startup still pays this latency. Metadata/prefix replacements weaken the qualification boundary; no cold-disk/startup performance claim.
Expose backend normal exit code or crash status without raw stderr. Runtime fixtures cover both exits and verify private stderr exclusion.
Remove unused headers and add the direct utility include.
Fail explicitly when canonical /tmp is absent before creating a temporary fixture, retaining canonical paths needed by launch validation.

Other source inputs unchanged.

corrected_failures: Fake Source teardown could run disconnected callbacks after its QPointer member was destroyed. Disconnect callbacks before member teardown; the observer suite then passes normally and under both sanitizers.

The initial optional plain-TUI test sent navigation input against the Codex loading draft. Reproduced literal escape echo; waiting for bracketed-paste mode and a loaded screen fixes the fixture. All final CLI cases pass. The added decoded mode field does not alter text decoding used by the already-passing live attention/history fixtures.
Worker-proposed receive cursor changes were discarded: installed Qt prefix removal advances its pointer. The original receive loop and reentrancy guards are retained.

delegation.route: CCR zai,glm-5.3; actual route and responses observed in router log
delegation.scope: Three disjoint worker assignments; service/transport handoffs reviewed and corrected. Observer worker was stopped for coordinator completion after proposed changes violated existing discovery/rebinding semantics. No worker self-report is used as test acceptance.

limits: macOS qualification only; no Linux UI claim.
Hash samples leave OS caches intact and are not cold-disk or whole-startup measurements. Full-file binary verification is retained.
Qt, Ghostty and platform libraries are not instrumented; sanitizer scope is the listed first-party suites and service fixtures.
No public protocol changes or automatic decision retries. PRs remain open; this receipt does not assert external review approval.
